title: Stock Coverage
text: Stock coverage estimates how long available inventory can support expected demand. A common formula is current stock divided by average daily unit sales. Lower coverage means greater stockout risk, but the result should be interpreted with seasonality, lead time and supplier constraints.

title: Reorder Point
text: A reorder point is the inventory level at which a replenishment order should be considered. A common approach is average demand during supplier lead time plus safety stock. A sales dataset without current stock, lead time or reorder settings cannot support a true reorder-point decision.

title: Gross Margin
text: Gross margin measures gross profit as a percentage of revenue. Gross profit is revenue minus cost of goods sold. Selling price alone is not enough to calculate gross profit or gross margin; cost data is required.

title: Sales Velocity
text: Sales velocity describes how quickly units or revenue are generated over time. Daily unit velocity can help compare demand across products, but it should be interpreted over an appropriate time window and with returns or cancellations considered.

title: Product Prioritization
text: Revenue concentration can help prioritize management attention. High-revenue products deserve monitoring, but revenue alone does not prove profitability because margin and costs may differ by product.

title: Retail KPIs
text: Useful retail KPIs include revenue, units sold, orders, average order value, product contribution, gross margin, stock coverage and stockout risk. KPIs should be calculated from source data rather than invented by an AI assistant.
